name: MegaBake overfitting audit
scope: Static audit (no GPU runs) of /workspace/megabake/src/megabake (compiler.py, plan.py, planner.py, schedule.py, regions.py, lowering.py, runtime.py, buckets.py, bodies/gemm.py, bodies/attention.py, bodies/generic.py, bodies/blackwell.py, fx_handler/hf_attention.py), benchmarks/stateful_models.py and benchmarks/full_model.py, tests/{unit,gpu,integration}, ROADMAP.md/PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md, git history (155 commits; tuned constants mostly introduced in a538d68 2026-10-16, e96e83f and bd40bf3 2026-10-17), the benchmark reports in artifacts/full_model*/ and the Mirage reference (agent_space/mirage/python/mirage/mpk/models/utils.py). Question answered: which compiler parameters, thresholds, tile sizes, worker counts, swapAB cutoffs, buckets, region matchers, stride heuristics, per-model wrappers, SM90/60-SM/BF16 assumptions and search budgets are generic, hardware-specific, or fitted to the tested models (SmolLM-135M/1.7B = Llama, Qwen2-0.5B, Gemma-3-270M, Qwen3.5-0.8B) and the H200 MIG 3g.71gb slice; what generic replacement each should get; and how well tests cover model families. Headline: the compiler core contains no model names (only comments), and worker count/SM count/shared memory come from device properties, but (1) for every real model (table launch) plan search is disabled (max_plans=1, max_compilations=1), so all performance choices are static constants; (2) the table-launch GEMM has exactly one tile config per launch (64x64x64, 8 stages, fixed 1 KiB+128 KiB+16 KiB smem, swapAB token tile 16/32/64 picked by max rows); (3) the interval-folding thresholds (2 rounds/phase, 6 rounds, 6 phases, 256 threads x 4 elements) cap folding at 2048-element maps and <=2-row reductions, which is exactly SmolLM-1.7B hidden size, so 4096-hidden models get no folding; (4) every tuned body is BF16-only and SM90a-only; (5) attention scratch caps KV length at 8192 keys and sliding windows are avoided rather than implemented; (6) GPU tests are almost exclusively the Llama/SmolLM fixture.

core_ideas.idea: Table-launch plan search is disabled for every real model
core_ideas.how_it_works: compile() switches to the table-driven launch when the graph has >1000 ops or >24 KB estimated kernel parameters; whenever that happens and the caller gave no budget it sets SearchBudget(max_plans=1, max_compilations=1). enumerate_body_selections then returns only the greedy seed (largest fused region first), worker count is min(work items, SMs x active blocks), and nothing is measured. All tested full models are table launches, so their plans are pure heuristics; the measured-search machinery (worker /2,/4 variants, 5% tie tolerance) only runs on small test graphs.

core_ideas.idea: Single fixed GEMM tile per table launch (64x64x64 BF16, 8 stages) with swapAB token tile 16/32/64
core_ideas.how_it_works: All table-launched GEMMs share one shared-memory layout TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES = 1 KiB barriers + 8 stages x (64x64 A + 64x64 B) BF16 + 4 x 64x32 epilogue. If every GEMM in the graph has <=64 rows, the launch uses swapAB (weight on WGMMA M=64, tokens on N) and the N tile is the smallest of (16,32,64) holding the largest row count; otherwise every GEMM uses a 64x64 tile. One orientation/tile serves every projection regardless of N, K or weight size, so e.g. lm_head (N=49152) and k_proj (N=64..512) get the same tile and stage count.

Originally 16 (Mirage linear_swapAB_hopper), raised to 64 in bd40bf3 so prompts/batches up to 64 rows stay on the small-M path. The crossover between swapAB and normal orientation was not measured per shape; 64 is the largest WGMMA N that fits the fixed smem budget, not a measured break-even. Above 64 rows the whole launch flips to 64x64 non-swapped tiles - this coincides with the documented prefill cliff above ~64 tokens.

core_ideas.idea: Split-K policy (SPLIT_K_MAX=16, SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES=2) gated by env var
core_ideas.how_it_works: split_k_count picks the largest split dividing K/64 that keeps tiles*splits <= SM count and >=2 K tiles per split. Off by default (MEGABAKE_SPLIT_K=1) because it gave 'no gain on the 60-SM slice'. The on/off decision is therefore a hardware-specific measurement baked in as a default; on a 132-SM H100/H200 or 148-SM B200 with the same small-N projections idle SMs double, so the conclusion likely flips.

core_ideas.idea: Interval folding thresholds (2 rounds per phase, 6 rounds, 6 phases)
core_ideas.how_it_works: A generic map/reduction body folds into its consumer's interval (recomputed per CTA, no barrier) only if single_cta_rounds <= 2, where a round = threads x MAP_ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD elements for maps (threads = max participating threads, 256 when a GEMM body exists -> 1024 elements) and = number of reduced rows for reductions; a run folds only if total <= 6 rounds and <= 6 phases. So maps of <=2048 elements and reductions of <=2 rows fold. 2048 is exactly SmolLM-1.7B hidden size; Qwen2-0.5B (896) and 135M (576) fit; Llama-3-8B (4096), Qwen2.5-7B (3584) or any batch>=3 decode get no RMSNorm folding. Limits were set while measuring 135M decode (11 -> ~6 intervals/layer) in bd40bf3.

core_ideas.idea: Worker count derived from device properties (generic)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Workers = min(max tile-map work items, multiprocessor_count x min maximum_active_blocks), from torch.cuda.get_device_properties. Measured search adds /2 and /4 variants (only when searching). This is the most generic piece; only the GEMM evidence metadata records 'max_admitted_workers: 60'.

core_ideas.idea: Split-context decode attention chunking (DECODE_MAX_CHUNKS=16, DECODE_MIN_CHUNK_KEYS=64, 0.15 pass penalty)
core_ideas.how_it_works: decode_chunks(rows, workers) minimises passes/chunks*(1+0.15*(passes-1)) over chunks<=min(16, workers); the kernel activates ceil(keys/64) chunks at runtime. The function form is generic (uses workers), but 0.15, 16 and 64 are hand-picked constants from 135M/1.7B long-context runs (a538d68); only engaged when head_dim % 32 == 0.

core_ideas.idea: Attention scratch limits (16 rows, 32 KiB) cap KV length at 8192
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each warp keeps one query row's FP32 scores in shared scratch; attention_scratch_rows = min(16, 32768 // (kv_length*4)) and the provider rejects when it is <1, i.e. kv_length > 8192 keys. 32 KiB is chosen to leave room next to the 145 KiB GEMM smem layout on SM90 (227 KiB). Long-context models fall back or fail.

G0 GEMM, bias epilogue, attention (score/prob dtype policy must be exactly BF16/FP32/BF16/FP32), kv_attention lowering and decode state shapes all require torch.bfloat16. FP16 or FP32 models silently fall to generic_contraction (one-thread-per-output scalar loop) and decomposed attention, which PERFORMANCE_REPORT measured 3-10 ms per GEMM at batch 256. FP8/INT4 weight-only models are not representable.

core_ideas.idea: SM90a-only tuned bodies and SM90-specific register/smem constants
core_ideas.how_it_works: G0 GEMM and attention providers reject anything but sm90a (attention is CUDA-core code but still gated on WGMMA). setmaxnreg 40/232 and 256 threads are the CUTLASS Hopper ping-pong layout; smem default get_smem_capacity_in_bytes('sm_90'); TargetFacts hard-codes max_registers_per_thread=255 and supports_tma=True; _target_facts rejects SM80/SM89 outright. Blackwell has a separate plain-GEMM provider only.

core_ideas.idea: Generic body constants (128 threads, 4 elements/thread, unroll 16)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Generated map/reduction bodies use 128-thread CTAs, 4 scalar (non-vectorized) elements per thread, full unroll when <=16 strided iterations. Chosen to make RMSNorm 5.0 -> 2.8 us on 1.7B. Not vectorized (no 128-bit loads), so efficiency depends on dtype width and hidden size multiples.

core_ideas.idea: Region matchers for RMSNorm / RoPE / attention / gated MLP
core_ideas.how_it_works: RMSNorm matcher is anchored on aten.mean.dim and requires pow.Tensor_Scalar -> mean -> add(scalar eps) -> rsqrt -> mul, optional cast, a weight multiply whose weight is a graph input, and optional residual add; the body is rebuilt from the captured scalar programs, so exponent/eps semantics are preserved (generic in semantics, Llama-shaped in structure). Gemma's x*(1+w) has a non-input weight operand, so the affine part stays a separate generic op [uncertain whether Dynamo keeps 1+w as runtime op]. LayerNorm (mean-subtracting, var_mean), Gemma-2/3 sqrt(dim) scaling, and L2-norm (gated delta) have no matcher and fall to generic reductions. RoPE matcher covers HF rotate_half and a cat-based layout (GPT-NeoX half-rotation); interleaved (GPT-J/Llama-original even/odd), partial rotary with pass-through only in one matcher, and M-RoPE are not recognised. Attention is primarily declared via HF AttentionInterface (generic); the ATen pattern fallback relies on a stride heuristic (_attention_head_axes) that previously misread size-1 MQA axes (fixed by the shape==1 special case). Gated MLP matcher recognises SiLU only and is always rejected (no paired-GEMM provider), so it is dead code today.

benchmarks/full_model.py routes model_type=='llama' to the hand-written StatefulSmolLM ('the tests and published numbers use'), attention-only HF models to the generic DecodeStep (AttentionInterface + pass-through cache), and hybrids to StatefulCausalLM which hard-codes Qwen3.5's interleaved output gate (detected by q_proj width == 2*heads*head_dim), Gemma sandwich norms (hasattr pre_feedforward_layernorm), the gated-delta-rule step in eager PyTorch with eps 1e-6, BF16 caches, batch 1, and refuses capacity > sliding_window. So published SmolLM numbers come from a per-model wrapper, not the generic path.

core_ideas.idea: Numerical acceptance tolerances tuned on SmolLM
core_ideas.how_it_works: Plan acceptance uses 1% relative L2 for small graphs, 2% for table launches (justified by the 30-layer SmolLM 1.6% drift) and teacher-forced 1% per region (justified by SmolLM-1.7B 4.2% end-to-end drift); bucketed prefill accepts 5%. Deeper or wider models drift more, so a fixed 2% will reject exact plans on 60+ layer models or accept small bugs on shallow ones.

Power-of-two buckets padded per call; each bucket is a separate static-shape compile. Max prompt 512 by default; compile time grows to 41 min for SmolLM-1.7B 512 bucket. Generic in form but the 512 cap and 64-row swapAB boundary are coupled to the tested short-prompt workloads.

core_ideas.idea: Table launch thresholds (1000 ops, 24 KB params)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Derived from CUDA's 32 KiB kernel-parameter limit (hardware/driver fact) with an estimate of 8+16*rank bytes per value; 1000-op cutoff is a heuristic proxy. Generic enough, but because it also gates search (above) and GEMM tile choice, crossing it changes plan quality qualitatively.

About 200 test functions. GPU end-to-end tests (test_task31_full_model, test_table_gemm) use only the SmolLM/Llama fixture (SmolLMArchitecture, StatefulSmolLM). Gemma3/Qwen3 appear only in CPU-level HF attention tests (tests/unit/test_hf_attention.py) and Qwen3.5/Gemma pointwise ops in test_pointwise_view_coverage. No GPU test for Qwen2 bias epilogue end to end, Gemma decode, MQA, head_dim 256 (Gemma), FP16, batch>1 decode, sliding windows, LayerNorm models (GPT-2/OPT/Phi), MoE, or non-H200 hardware; test_gemm_range_body asserts compute capability (9,0).

megabake_status.notes: Classification: overfit-by-omission (no tuning at all for real models). Generic replacement: keep search but make it cheap - analytic cost model (bytes moved / achievable BW + barrier count x measured barrier cost + per-phase dispatch) to rank candidates, then measure top-k with the existing PlanEvaluator; cache results keyed by (graph hash, device name, SM count, clocks).

megabake_status.idea: Single fixed GEMM tile per table launch
megabake_status.notes: Classification: hardware-specific (sized for SM90 227 KiB smem minus attention scratch) and shape-agnostic. Generic replacement: per-GEMM tile candidates (N tile 16..256, K tile 64/128, stages from smem budget) with a smem layout = max over chosen configs, chosen by nvMatmulHeuristics-style analytic model or a micro-autotune at compile time; allow per-phase orientation since descriptors are already written per phase.

Classification: hardware-specific (WGMMA N granularity, smem budget) with a model/workload-fitted cutoff. Generic replacement: decide orientation per GEMM from a roofline: swapAB when rows < WGMMA M (64) and weight bytes dominate; token tile = smallest legal WGMMA N (multiples of 8/16) >= rows; above 64 rows use normal tiles per GEMM rather than flipping the whole launch.

Classification: hardware-specific decision measured on 60 SMs. Generic replacement: enable by cost model - split when output tiles < SM count x occupancy and K/64 >= 2*splits; include reduction cost; validate on 132/148-SM parts.

Classification: model-overfit (cap = 2048 elements = SmolLM-1.7B hidden; reductions <=2 rows). Generic replacement: fold when estimated recompute time (elements x bytes / per-SM bandwidth + latency rounds) < barrier cost (measure grid barrier once per device at compile time) - i.e., compare two costs instead of counting rounds; scale with batch and hidden size.
Classification: generic. Keep; only the evidence metadata 'max_admitted_workers: 60' is stale documentation.

Classification: partly generic (uses workers), constants (16, 64, 0.15) fitted. Generic replacement: derive 0.15 from measured barrier/exchange latency vs per-key time (keys x head_dim x 2 x 2 bytes / per-SM BW); allow head_dim not multiple of 32 via masked lanes.

Classification: hardware-specific + workload-fitted (short contexts). Generic replacement: online softmax over KV tiles (flash-decoding) so scratch is O(tile), independent of kv_length; size scratch from target.max_shared_memory_per_cta minus GEMM layout.

Classification: model-overfit (all tested checkpoints run in bf16). Generic replacement: parametrise element type (FP16/BF16 trivially in CUTLASS; FP8 E4M3 with scales on SM90; FP32 accum unchanged), and make the attention numerical policy a parameter rather than a literal dict.

Classification: hardware-specific. Generic replacement: TargetFacts should carry smem per SM, register file, TMA/WGMMA/tcgen05 flags, cluster support from device query or a per-arch table; attention/generic bodies should not require WGMMA; add an SM80 mma.sync GEMM path.

Classification: hardware-generic-ish, not model-tuned, but untuned. Generic replacement: vector width = 16 bytes / dtype size, elements/thread chosen so tiles divide the innermost dim; autotune threads per CTA in {128,256} with the cost model.

Classification: model-overfit in structure (HF Llama/Qwen RMSNorm and rotate_half RoPE). Generic replacement: replace pattern-specific matchers by a generic 'row-reduction + broadcast epilogue' fusion (any reduction over the last axis followed by elementwise consumers of the same row), which covers RMSNorm, LayerNorm, Gemma (1+w), L2-norm, softmax; express RoPE as generic gather/select elementwise; extend declared ops (megabake::rms_norm, rope) via HF/vLLM-style custom ops for the remainder.

Classification: model-specific. Generic replacement: retire StatefulSmolLM for Llama (DecodeStep already handles it) so published numbers use the generic path; declare gated delta rule and other stateful mixers as ops (ROADMAP step 6) instead of StatefulCausalLM detection heuristics; implement sliding windows in kv_attention (ring buffer or mask by valid_length-window).

Classification: model-overfit (constants justified by SmolLM depth). Generic replacement: keep teacher-forced per-region verification as the primary check with tolerance derived from dtype epsilon x sqrt(reduction length); end-to-end check scaled with depth or replaced by per-region checks only.

Classification: generic form, workload-fitted range. Generic replacement: buckets derived from GEMM tile breakpoints (swapAB N tiles, 64/128 M tiles) and user max length; ultimately dynamic sequence length via runtime tile counts.
Classification: generic (driver param limit), 1000-op proxy heuristic. Replacement: decide purely on computed parameter bytes; decouple search budget from this switch.

Classification: overfit coverage. Replacement: parametrised tiny-config GPU tests for Llama, Qwen2 (bias), Qwen3 (q/k norm), Gemma3 (MQA, head_dim 256, sandwich norm, sliding), Phi/GPT-NeoX (LayerNorm, partial rotary), Mistral (sliding window), MoE (OLMoE/Qwen3-MoE tiny), FP16 variant, batch 2-8 decode; per-region bit-exact checks run on random weights.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities: Compile-time autotuning of whole-kernel schedule: because the entire model is one kernel with a static phase table, MegaBake can measure the real end-to-end kernel (barriers, L2 reuse across phases, tile interference) for each candidate plan, which a multi-kernel graph tuner (Inductor max-autotune, Triton autotune) cannot: they tune each kernel in isolation and miss cross-kernel effects such as L2 residency and launch gaps. Nearest multi-kernel substitute: per-kernel autotuning plus CUDA Graph capture, which ignores inter-kernel interactions. Currently unused because table launches force max_plans=1.

Device-calibrated barrier-vs-recompute folding: only a persistent kernel has grid barriers whose cost can be traded against redundant per-CTA recompute; making the fold decision a cost comparison (barrier_us vs recompute_us) generalises across models and SM counts. Multi-kernel graphs pay a kernel boundary (~2-4 us with graphs, ~1 us with PDL) and can only fuse via Inductor's vertical fusion, not recompute-instead-of-sync.

Per-phase GEMM orientation/tile in one launch: TMA descriptors are already written per phase in the prologue, so different tile shapes per projection are possible if the smem layout is the max over configs; separate kernels get this for free, but in a megakernel it must be designed into the smem budget - the current single-layout simplification is the main source of shape overfitting.

Runtime-adaptive split decisions: the persistent kernel knows valid_length at runtime (decode_chunks already uses in_use chunks), so split-K/split-context factors can be chosen per call without relaunching - a CUDA graph freezes grid sizes at capture.
measured_or_reported_gains: From MegaBake docs (H200 MIG 3g.71gb, 60 SMs, bf16, batch 1): swapAB raised 1.7B decode GEMMs from 0.84-1.04 to 1.78-2.07 TB/s (3.66 -> 1.92 ms GEMM time; ROADMAP.md:118); interval folding cut 135M decode barriers 333 -> 183 (-5-7% on 135M but only -1-2% on 1.7B, consistent with the 2048-element fold cap; ROADMAP.md:146); split-K 'no gain on the 60-SM slice'; split-context decode 135M at 2000 cached tokens 22.7 -> 2.3 ms. Fresh decode kernel times (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18): 135M 1.50 ms, 1.7B 2.97 ms, Qwen2-0.5B 1.58 ms; Qwen3.5-0.8B prefill fails (aten.cumsum); older artifacts: Gemma-3-270M decode 2.08 ms, gemma-2b 3.59 ms. External: NVIDIA reports nvMatmulHeuristics shortlists let CUTLASS reach near-exhaustive-autotune performance while profiling only a few candidates [uncertain - exact numbers not verified in this audit]. Mirage MPK itself is also per-model tuned (grid 96/64 hard-coded in mpk/models/utils.py).
expected_impact_on_megabake:
Ranked by impact on generality and performance (estimates, no GPU runs):
1. Re-enable cost-model-guided search for table launches: the plan for every real model is currently the greedy seed. A cost model + top-3 measured candidates per model would mostly protect against regressions on unseen shapes; on tested models expected gain 0-5% decode [uncertain], but on new shapes (e.g., N not multiple of 64, large vocab) it avoids worst-case tile choices. Compile time +3 builds (~20 s each for 1.7B).
2. Cost-based interval folding: for a 4096-hidden model at batch 1 the current cap folds nothing of the hidden-size maps/norms; each layer would pay ~11 barrier intervals (~0.7 us each) instead of ~6, i.e. +3.5 us/layer = +112 us on a 32-layer 8B model (~2-3% of a ~4.5 ms weight-bound step on 60 SMs). On 1.7B, raising the MLP-activation map cap (8192 elements) could save 1 interval/layer = 24 x 0.7 = ~17 us (~0.6%).
3. Per-GEMM tile/orientation and prefill >64 rows: the prefill cliff (3-21x slower than Inductor+CUDA graphs at 128-300 tokens) is partly caused by the whole launch flipping to 64x64 tiles with 1 CTA per SM and no per-GEMM tile choice; per-GEMM 128x128/128x256 tiles for M>=128 could recover a large fraction (2-5x prefill at 128-512 tokens) [uncertain].
4. FP16/FP8 dtype parametrisation: zero gain on tested bf16 models, but without it any fp16 checkpoint falls to generic_contraction (measured 3-10 ms per GEMM at batch 256 vs ~0.01 ms tuned) - a 100x cliff.
5. Split-K enabled by cost model: ~0 on 60 SMs (measured), likely 5-15% decode GEMM time on 132-SM H100/H200 where small projections (k/v_proj N=320-1024 -> 5-16 tiles) leave >90% of SMs idle [uncertain].
6. Attention without the 8192-key cap: 0 on tested short contexts; prevents compile failure/fallback for long-context use.
7. Tolerances derived from dtype/depth: no speed impact; avoids false rejections on deeper models (>30 layers).
generality_and_overfitting_risk:
MODEL-OVERFIT (fitted to SmolLM/Qwen2-class small dense bf16 Llama-style models):
- Fold thresholds _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PHASE=2/_FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS=6/_FOLD_MAX_PHASES=6 with 256 threads x MAP_ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD=4 (src/megabake/schedule.py:1383-1386, bodies/generic.py:441): fold cap = 2048 elements = SmolLM-1.7B hidden size; reductions fold only for <=2 rows (batch<=2 decode). Set while tuning 135M decode (bd40bf3).
- Numerical tolerances 0.01/0.02/0.01 and bucket 0.05 (compiler.py:236-248, buckets.py:42) justified in comments by 30-layer SmolLM and SmolLM-1.7B drift.
- BF16-only literal checks in GEMM, bias, attention numerical policy, kv_attention lowering, DecodeStep state (gemm.py:1814-1820, :1938; attention.py:107-140; lowering.py:1864-1866; hf_attention.py:174).
- RMSNorm matcher structure = HF LlamaRMSNorm (regions.py:686-819; comment at :750 names LlamaRMSNorm); Gemma (1+w) affine and LayerNorm unmatched; RoPE matchers = HF rotate_half; gated-MLP matcher SiLU-only and dead (regions.py:2240).
- Attention head-axis stride heuristic (regions.py:1250-1264) already broke on Gemma 3 MQA (ROADMAP.md:34) - a sign the ATen fallback path is fitted to the shapes seen.
- Decode wrappers: StatefulSmolLM for llama (benchmarks/full_model.py:173-184) means published Llama numbers do not exercise the generic DecodeStep; StatefulCausalLM hard-codes Qwen3.5 gate detection by projection width and Gemma sandwich norms by attribute name (benchmarks/stateful_models.py:78-83, :153-157); sliding window avoided by refusing capacity > window (hf_attention.py:128-132).
- Attention KV cap 8192 and split-context constants 16/64/0.15 (attention.py:258-271, :422-423, :748) fitted to <=2k-context benchmarks.
- Buckets max 512 (buckets.py:38) fitted to short prompts.
HARDWARE-SPECIFIC (SM90 / 60-SM slice):
- TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES single layout (gemm.py:1711), 64x64x64 tile, 8 stages, setmaxnreg 40/232, 256 threads, smem capacity 'sm_90' (gemm.py:216-220), providers reject non-sm90a (gemm.py:1847, attention.py:220).
- SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64 / (16,32,64) and split-K off by default ('no gain on the 60-SM slice', ROADMAP.md:149) - decisions measured on 60 SMs at ~2.2 TB/s; on 132 SMs the balance between per-SM bandwidth and tile count changes.
- _target_facts: arch allow-list excludes SM80/SM89, max_registers_per_thread=255 and supports_tma=True literals (compiler.py:1502-1514).
- Evidence metadata records max_admitted_workers=60 and microsecond timings from this device (gemm.py:2232-2238) - harmless metadata but should not be used as policy.
GENERIC:
- Worker count from SM count x occupancy (schedule.py:1365-1378); table-launch switch based on parameter bytes (compiler.py:213-224); split_k_count divisibility logic; decode_chunks form; declared megabake::attention via HF AttentionInterface (fx_handler/hf_attention.py) - covers every HF attention model; RMSNorm body rebuilt from captured scalar programs (semantics generic).
HOW REFERENCE SYSTEMS AVOID IT: CUTLASS/cuBLAS use nvMatmulHeuristics (analytic per-SKU ranking + profile shortlist); Triton autotune uses prune_configs_by {perf_model, top_k}; Inductor max-autotune benchmarks template choices per shape; TVM MetaSchedule/Ansor use learned cost models + search. Mirage MPK is NOT a counter-example - its builders are per model and utils.py hard-codes 96/64 grids 'enough to cover all Qwen3 model'. MegaBake already has the measured-search scaffolding (plan.py SearchBudget, PlanEvaluator, plan cache) - the overfitting comes from bypassing it for table launches and from fixed constants in providers.
hardware_portability: SM90-bound: TMA+WGMMA G0 GEMM (CUTLASS HopperWgmmaGemmPersistentKernel), setmaxnreg 40/232 warp specialisation, swapAB via WGMMA N tiles, 227 KiB smem layout. SM100: needs tcgen05/TMEM GEMM (bodies/blackwell.py has a plain unbiased GEMM provider only - no swapAB, bias or table-launch integration), larger smem (228 KiB on B200, ~100 KiB on SM120 consumer parts) so TABLE_GEMM_SHARED_BYTES (~145 KiB) would not even fit on SM120. SM80/SM89: rejected outright by _target_facts; would need mma.sync/cp.async GEMM; grid barrier, table launch, generic bodies, attention (CUDA-core) and split-context are portable in principle - attention is unnecessarily gated on WGMMA. To stay target-generic: (1) TargetFacts from device query plus a per-arch capability table (smem/SM, regs, TMA, WGMMA, tcgen05, cluster, CLC); (2) providers declare requirements and the planner picks; (3) all tile/stage/smem constants computed from TargetFacts and the chosen per-GEMM configs; (4) calibrate barrier latency, per-SM bandwidth and HBM bandwidth with micro-benchmarks once per device at compile time and feed the cost model; (5) keep measured search as the final arbiter, cached per (device name, SM count, MIG profile).

2. Where is the true swapAB vs normal crossover per GEMM shape on 60 vs 132 SMs? Experiment: standalone sweep rows 1..256 x (N,K) of tested projections with both orientations and tiles 16/32/64/128.
3. Would raising fold caps help 1.7B (MLP activation 8192 elements)? Experiment: tools/phase_profile.py with _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PHASE in {2,4,8} on 1.7B and a 4096-hidden model (e.g., tiny-layer Llama-3-8B config with 2 layers).
4. Is split-K beneficial on a full 132-SM H200? Experiment: MEGABAKE_SPLIT_K=1 vs 0 on full GPU.
5. Does Dynamo/AOT keep Gemma's (1+weight) as a runtime op so the RMSNorm affine is left unfused? Experiment: dump regions (dump_region_graph) for Gemma-3-270M decode.
6. How does accuracy drift scale with depth for >30-layer models under the 2% limit? Experiment: 2-, 30-, 60-layer random-weight Llama configs, teacher-forced vs end-to-end error.
7. Is register reallocation (setmaxnreg decrease to 40) safe for generic bodies that follow a GEMM phase (PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:287)? Experiment: compute-sanitizer/racecheck and SASS inspection.
